teaser: Today, we're exploring a phrase that expresses the hope for all things to go smoothly.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Today, we're exploring a phrase that expresses the hope for all things to go smoothly. [break 1s] The phrase is: 万事如意, wàn shì rú yì. [break 1s] 万 (wàn) means ‘ten thousand’ or ‘all’; [break 0.5s] 事 (shì) means ‘things’ or ‘affairs’; [break 0.5s] 如 (rú) means ‘like’ or ‘as’; [break 0.5s] 意 (yì) means ‘will’ or ‘desire’. [break 1s] So, 万事如意 literally means ‘all things as you wish’, and figuratively it conveys the meaning of everything goes as you wish. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom has roots in traditional Chinese culture, where expressing good wishes for others was very common. It often appears during celebrations, such as weddings, to convey hopes for a happy and successful life. The phrase captures the essence of optimism and well-wishing, making it a staple in greetings and blessings. [break 1.5s] For our first example: 祝你万事如意！ [break 1s] Wishing you all your desires come true! [break 1s] For the second example: 在新年期间，大家都说万事如意。 [break 1s] During the New Year, everyone says, 'May all things go smoothly.' [break 1s] And for the third example: 他的生意越来越好，真是万事如意。 [break 1s] His business is getting better and better; truly everything goes as he wishes. [break 1s] So, remember, 万事如意 means 'everything goes as you wish.' Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.
